messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 detected: canary p95 latency spike + kernel_fallback surge for runtime-edge v3.7.0 at 2026-03-15T09:45Z. Alert: https://dash.redwood.dev/alerts/2147489000

deploy-bot: Canary started 2026-03-15T09:30Z -> runtime-edge:v3.7.0 receiving 15% of traffic in canary pool

alice: saw the alert, p95 shot from ~85ms -> ~430ms on the canary slice. spinning up collection and attaching traces.

ben: telemetry shows kernel_fallback_count jump to ~27% across g5x-affinity hosts. batching_latency and batch_size distributions skewed down (more single-token execs).

carol: tagging @eng-sre and runtime owners. @tom-pager can you take SRE lead? @bjorn from runtime can you look at kernel selector logs?

essential-logs-bot: Logs bundle uploaded: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2147489000/canary-bundle-0948.tar.gz

tom: oncall here. correlating host metrics now. A subset of canary pods shows batch_manager timeouts increasing, queue lengths spike, and a flurry of kernel:fallback decisions. suspect routing heuristic in v3.7.0.

alice: proxy excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T09:44:18Z WARN route: routing-heuristic=v3.7 pick kernel=fallback model=open-ggml-7b seq_len=1024
2026-03-15T09:44:18Z WARN batch: timeout extended 5ms->58ms
```

ben: Found config diff in the rollout manifest: feature flag new-routing-heuristic=true was enabled for canary. PR: https://git.redwood.dev/runtime/changes/PR-514 (recent change to kernel affinity scoring)

carol: can we toggle the flag off in canary as an immediate mitigation? if this is causing suboptimal kernel picks, kill-switch now.

alice: executing kill-switch for new-routing-heuristic scoped to canary via admin API:
```
POST /admin/flags/kill
{ "flag": "new-routing-heuristic", "scope": "canary", "value": "false" }
```

deploy-bot: Feature flag new-routing-heuristic set to false for scope=canary by alice at 2026-03-15T09:50:05

tom: monitoring after flag flip. kernel_fallback rates dropping to ~6% on canary hosts. p95 improved from 430ms -> ~120ms but still above baseline. Holding 5m to watch for stabilization.

oncall-maria: quick customer-impact note: CS spikes for EU prefixes show increased error logs and some 502s between 09:44-09:51. CS Ops pinged, estimated affected requests ~2% concentrated on high-seq multi-turn workloads. Opening incident ticket in CS queue.

ben: also seeing elevated KV cache churn coincident with routing changes; new shard placement may have increased cache misses and amplified tail latency.

alice: consensus: abort rollout and roll the canary back to v3.6.4. Deploy team, initiate rollback playbook for canary, stop further promotion to prod.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: target version set to v3.6.4; canary traffic will be drained over 2 minutes.

bjorn: starting rollback now. patching canary deployment image->runtime-edge:v3.6.4. kubectl rollout restart applied.

bjorn: new pods coming up; readiness checks passing on 6/6 nodes.

tom: traffic drain complete. kernel_fallback metrics back to baseline; p95 around ~95ms now. marking canary incident mitigated.

oncall-maria: handing off to post-deploy reviews and customer ops. @cs-ops please monitor the 4 customers flagged and update incident ticket. Creating postmortem channel: #postmortem-2147489000

alice: mitigation summary for timeline:
- disabled feature flag new-routing-heuristic in canary
- rolled back canary to v3.6.4
- gathered logs/metrics snapshot and uploaded to S3

ben: preliminary root cause hypothesis: the routing heuristic change in v3.7.0 altered kernel affinity scoring causing more long-context requests to be routed to kernels that don't batch well, triggering kernel fallback. secondary: changed shard placements raised KV cache miss rate, worsening tail latency.

carol: customer impact: small number of EU multi-turn customers affected (low volume, high seq). CS currently tracking 4 reported incidents, no billing anomalies reported.

bjorn: immediate action items (short):
- runtime team to reproduce with seq-heavy prompts and validate kernel selection logic (owner: bjorn)
- eng-sre to add a canary rollout guard: alert if kernel_fallback_rate > 5% within first 10m (owner: tom)
- product-ops to add active probes for high-sequence flows during rollouts (owner: maria)

alice: longer term: build a rollout-test harness that runs representative high-seq prompts against routing heuristics before enabling flags at canary. scheduling follow-up.

deploy-bot: Incident annotated: mitigation recorded at 2026-03-15T09:55:40. Postmortem channel created: #postmortem-2147489000

oncall-maria: will continue monitoring for 6 hours, updating postmortem with detailed timeline and affected prefixes. Thanks all for quick response. :white_check_mark:
